\begin{tablenotes}[flushleft]
\footnotesize
\item \textit{Notes:} Pooled: one model fitted on all 48 half-hour bars of the day, read at the 16:00 bar; per-bar:
fitted on the 16:00 bar alone; both pre-tuned, on the same inputs and days. $\Delta$QLIKE: per-bar mean QLIKE over
pooled, minus 1, in \%; DM: Diebold--Mariano statistic of the daily QLIKE difference (Harvey--Leybourne--Newbold
corrected, automatic Newey--West lag), negative when the per-bar fit is more accurate. Mid: the straddle is bought or sold at the 15:30 midpoint; crossed: a buy pays the ask and a sale receives the bid, the spread paid at entry only (settlement is cash at intrinsic). Sharpe ratio $=\sqrt{252}\,\bar r/\mathrm{sd}(r)$, annualised per trade day (the trade runs about 200 days a year).
Every $t$ is Newey--West (Bartlett kernel, lag $\lfloor 1.5\,n^{1/3}\rfloor = 14$ at $n = 866$); the $t$ of a $\Delta$Sharpe is that of the mean daily return difference, so it tests the mean difference, not the Sharpe difference. Bold: $|t| > 1.96$ (5\,\%, two-sided), on the estimate and its $t$. Bold DM: $|\mathrm{DM}| > 1.96$.
\end{tablenotes}
